articles.headline: PHEV Emissions Significantly Higher Than Official Ratings, Study Finds
articles.dek: Real-world data shows plug-in hybrid vehicles emit nearly six times more than reported, prompting calls for regulatory adjustments and revised taxation.
articles.lead: New analysis of 2024 real-world data reveals a substantial discrepancy between the official emissions ratings of plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs) and their actual performance. On average, PHEVs emitted nearly six times more than their reported figures, a gap that has widened due to a market shift towards heavier, more powerful, and longer-range models with insufficient electric motor capacity.
articles.takeaway: Real-world data shows plug-in hybrid vehicles emit nearly six times more than reported, prompting calls for regulatory adjustments and revised taxation.
body: New analysis of 2024 real-world data reveals a substantial discrepancy between the official emissions ratings of plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs) and their actual performance. On average, PHEVs emitted nearly six times more than their reported figures, a gap that has widened due to a market shift towards heavier, more powerful, and longer-range models with insufficient electric motor capacity.

The findings highlight the critical need for the upcoming November 2026/27 utility factor (UF) correction, designed to align official accounting with real-world climate impact and encourage improved vehicle performance. Evidence from a previous UF correction in 2025 suggests that such adjustments can lead to reduced CO2 emissions through technological advancements and extended electric ranges.

However, current taxation policies in most EU Member States do not adequately differentiate between high-emitting PHEVs and those with superior performance. This lack of distinction, coupled with company car purchases dominating the PHEV market, means that less efficient models often receive preferential treatment.

Analysis indicates that PHEVs are driven in pure electric mode only 27% of the time. Models with longer electric ranges, exceeding 70 km, exhibited a larger emissions gap compared to shorter-range vehicles. Conversely, PHEVs with a higher ratio of electric to combustion power demonstrate significantly lower real-world emissions.

Recent PHEV models launched after the 2025 UF correction show manufacturers are increasing electric range and battery size to offset the impact of UF adjustments. This has led to improved efficiency, with increased battery size only marginally affecting vehicle price. Projections suggest that electric ranges of 140–220 km will be necessary for PHEVs to remain at or below 50 gCO2/km by 2030.

The study urges European co-legislators to uphold the planned UF correction, emphasizing that it is a technical methodology to ensure accurate emissions reporting. It also recommends that taxation systems be revised to incorporate stricter CO2 and electric-range criteria, ensuring that better-performing PHEVs are appropriately rewarded.

attribution.originalTitle: Still Smoking: The PHEV Emissions Scandal Continues

faqs.question: What is the main issue with current PHEV emissions reporting?
faqs.answer: Real-world emissions for PHEVs are significantly higher than officially reported figures, with average emissions nearly six times greater than WLTP test values.

faqs.question: What is the proposed solution to address the PHEV emissions gap?
faqs.answer: The upcoming November 2026/27 utility factor correction aims to align official reporting with real-world performance, and taxation policies should be updated to better incentivize higher-performing PHEVs.

articles.headline: Denmark's EV Transition Reshapes Fossil Fuel Ecosystem
articles.dek: As electric vehicles dominate new car sales in Denmark, traditional automotive services and infrastructure face significant disruption.
articles.lead: Denmark is experiencing a rapid shift in its automotive landscape, with electric vehicles (EVs) now constituting 97% of new private vehicle sales. This transition is prompting a reevaluation of the entire fossil fuel ecosystem, from repair shops to fuel stations.
articles.takeaway: As electric vehicles dominate new car sales in Denmark, traditional automotive services and infrastructure face significant disruption.
body: Denmark is experiencing a rapid shift in its automotive landscape, with electric vehicles (EVs) now constituting 97% of new private vehicle sales. This transition is prompting a reevaluation of the entire fossil fuel ecosystem, from repair shops to fuel stations.

Mechanics in Denmark are adapting to the rise of EVs, with new training courses emerging for EV repair. While basic maintenance like brakes, tires, and suspension remain similar, the core components of internal combustion engines and gearboxes are being replaced by electric drivetrains and battery packs. This requires specialized tools and advanced diagnostic skills, moving beyond traditional mechanical expertise.

Businesses that relied heavily on internal combustion engine (ICE) services, such as muffler shops and those specializing in oil changes, are expected to decline. The need for routine maintenance on EVs is generally lower than on ICE vehicles, with some manufacturers extending service intervals. This necessitates a transformation for mechanics into highly skilled technicians capable of advanced diagnostics and component optimization.

The impact extends to the fuel retail sector as well. With the majority of EV charging occurring at home, the market for public charging stations is becoming more competitive, leading to predictions that many traditional gas stations may disappear.

This transformation in Denmark mirrors trends across Scandinavia, with Norway, Sweden, and Finland also showing significant adoption rates for EVs. The shift is not limited to passenger cars, as these countries are also moving towards zero-emission freight vehicles, further signaling the decline of the petrochemical ecosystem.

faqs.question: How are mechanics adapting to the rise of EVs in Denmark?
faqs.answer: Mechanics are undergoing retraining for EV-specific repairs and diagnostics, and workshops are adapting their services and signage to reflect the shift.

faqs.answer: With most EV charging happening at home, gas stations are facing increased competition for the smaller public charging market, leading to expectations of closures.

articles.takeaway: The electric SUV sees a $300 price hike across base and sportier trims, with the LT model now starting above $45,000.
body: Chevrolet has raised the starting price for the 2027 Blazer EV, with the base LT trim now beginning at over $45,000. This represents a $300 increase from the previous model year. Including the mandatory $1,795 destination fee, the 2027 Blazer EV LT has a starting Manufacturer's Suggested Retail Price (MSRP) of $46,795.

The sportier RS trim also experiences a $300 price increase, bringing its starting MSRP to $52,595. The top-tier SS trim's price remains unchanged at $62,495. All-wheel-drive (AWD) is an additional $3,000 for the LT and RS models, while the SS trim comes standard with AWD.

The 2027 Blazer EV LT and RS models are equipped with an 85 kWh battery, offering an EPA-estimated range of up to 312 miles for front-wheel-drive (FWD) configurations and 283 miles for AWD versions. The SS trim features a larger 102 kWh battery, providing an estimated range of up to 302 miles.

All new 2027 General Motors electric vehicles, including the Blazer EV, now feature a native NACS port, allowing direct use of Tesla Superchargers. An optional eight-speaker premium Bose sound system is also available for the LT and RS trims, a feature previously exclusive to the SS model. Despite the price increase, the Blazer EV remains competitively positioned against some rivals, though it is longer and offers more interior space than certain competitors.

attribution.originalTitle: Chevy hikes Blazer EV prices, pushing it over $45,000

faqs.question: What is the starting price for the 2027 Chevy Blazer EV LT?
faqs.answer: The 2027 Chevy Blazer EV LT starts at $46,795, including the destination fee.

faqs.question: What is the maximum EPA-estimated range for the 2027 Chevy Blazer EV?
faqs.answer: The FWD LT and RS models offer an EPA-estimated range of up to 312 miles.
